title: 🛡️ The Wolfroad Compact
description: A sworn courier crosses a divided march with a dead king's last compact, bargaining through noble halls, river towns, border camps, and old hill oaths before civil war closes the roads.

nodes.label: Last Writ
text: King Maelor dies in a shuttered hunting lodge while rain claws at the roof. Lady Maerla Veyne presses his sealed compact into your hands before the candles gutter. 📜
You are Ren Arlen, sworn courier and minor sword-bearer, suddenly worth more alive than any banner in Harrowmere.

nodes.label: Oath Choice
text: Maerla's guards listen from the doorway. The compact would place Princess Elowen under a council of rivals, denying every house the single prize they expected.
Maerla asks whether your oath still has legs enough for one last road.

nodes.label: Oath Taken
text: You kneel on wet rushes and swear by the dead king's hand. Maerla gives one sharp nod, as if gratitude is a coin she cannot safely spend.

nodes.label: Hard Price
text: You ask what this road will cost. Maerla answers, "Friends, sleep, and perhaps the clean idea you have of loyalty."
The honesty is almost generous.

nodes.label: Paid Courier
text: You name a price. Maerla pays from a small iron box, then warns that silver has a louder voice than vows when men start counting motives.

nodes.label: Four Roads
text: By dawn, Harrowmere opens before you: the Wolfroad north, the river market east, Hollow Abbey in the hills, and Red Ford where soldiers wait hungry.
Highmere lies beyond them all, but arriving empty-handed would only feed the claimants.

nodes.label: North Gate
text: You ride beneath pines heavy with rain. Northmen have tied strips of black wool to the branches, each one a promise that Lord Garran Brant remembers insults.

nodes.label: River Gate
text: You turn toward the flat road where barges, tollmen, and fishwives carry rumor faster than horses. The compact lies warm against your ribs.

nodes.label: Abbey Gate
text: The hill path climbs toward Hollow Abbey, where royal oaths are copied in brown ink and older promises are kept under stone.

nodes.label: Road Weather
text: The Wolfroad narrows between wet pines. Hoofprints cross and recross until the mud looks argued over.
Weather, men, and chance decide what reaches you first.

nodes.label: Clear Mile
text: For one merciful mile the road stays empty. You use the quiet to check the seal, count your food, and listen for pursuit that does not come.

nodes.label: Broken Cart
text: A crofter's cart has broken an axle in the ditch. You lift before asking names, and the family presses smoked barley into your saddlebag in thanks.

nodes.label: Toll Patrol
text: A Brant patrol stops you under a leaning ash. Their sergeant studies your gloves too long, then waves you on with the sour look of a man remembering faces.

nodes.label: Pine Camp
text: At a hunter's camp, three paths split from the coals. One climbs toward Wolfhall's banners, one turns to an abandoned watch, and one returns south before the north notices you twice.

nodes.label: Bannered Keep
text: Wolfhall rises from a ridge of black stone, all wet banners and narrow windows. No wolf needs to howl here; the keep itself has teeth enough.

nodes.label: Keep Yard
text: Stablehands stop talking when they see you. Men in ringmail crowd the yard, and above them Lord Garran's red shield hangs over the great doors.

nodes.label: Steel Courtesy
text: You show Maelor's seal openly. The captain at the stair bows with perfect hatred and sends a runner ahead, making sure half the keep knows you came.

nodes.label: Spear Work
text: You help haul a wagon of spearheads from the rain. Soldiers respect useful hands, and one tells you Lord Garran has been promised more than he admits.

nodes.label: Servant Door
text: You follow the laundry steam through a side passage and pocket a small iron key from a forgotten hook. The passage smells of soap, fear, and supper smoke.

nodes.label: Lord Garran
text: Lord Garran Brant receives you beside a hearth big enough to roast an ox. His beard is silver, his hands are scarred, and his courtesy arrives armored.

nodes.label: Hidden Gallery
text: Behind the hall's carved screen, Lady Ilyra Brant tells a steward that her father is being fed forged raid reports. She sounds angry enough to be useful.

nodes.label: Hard Terms
text: You speak of a council that would preserve his honor. Garran says honor is often a cloak sewn by men standing far from winter roads.

nodes.label: Raid Charge
text: You accuse his riders of striking villages to force the council. Garran's fist hits the table; a cup breaks, and a shard cuts your palm before anyone moves.

nodes.label: Ilyra's Word
text: Lady Ilyra meets you in the hawk court. She gives you a silver brooch shaped like a broken shield and says the false orders passed through her father's steward.

nodes.label: Supper Turn
text: Supper begins under antlers, sword belts, and servants pretending not to hear. Every cup raised to the dead king seems to ask who will own his daughter.

nodes.label: Guest Bread
text: Ilyra breaks guest bread with you before the hall. In the north, that small act makes murder inconvenient and friendship at least plausible. 🍞

nodes.label: Open Insult
text: A young knight calls couriers leashed ravens. You answer mildly enough to keep the peace, sharply enough that the old captains laugh into their cups.

nodes.label: Low Whisper
text: A kitchen boy slips you a folded note meant for the steward. It names a hostage kept at Red Ford and a payment due after the council vote.

nodes.label: Postern Choice
text: By midnight, Wolfhall has shown you smiles, knives, and doors. The steward's chamber lies above the buttery, while Garran's riders wait in the yard.

nodes.label: Ledger Rumor
text: A frightened scullion points you toward the steward's chest and begs you not to say who knew. Fear moves through this keep with better manners than servants.

nodes.label: Wolf Escort
text: Garran lends two riders with old scars and careful eyes. Their banner makes some gates easier and some conversations much more dangerous.

nodes.label: Pine Forage
text: The old watch is half-swallowed by pine roots. You search its stones while rain ticks through the broken roof.

nodes.label: Bitter Herbs
text: Under the watch stair you find wintergreen and woundwort wrapped in waxed cloth by someone who expected to return and never did.

nodes.label: Bandit Arrows
text: Men with hunting bows try your purse from the treeline. You drive them off, but one arrow tears your sleeve and leaves a hot line beneath it.

nodes.label: South Again
text: You leave Wolfhall with wet boots and more eyes behind you than before. The compact remains sealed, but the north has pressed its thumb into the wax.

nodes.label: Steward Chest
text: The steward's chamber is narrow, warm, and locked badly. A black ledger sits under folded linens, its clasp stamped with three houses that should not agree.

nodes.label: Purchased Ledger
text: Silver opens the steward faster than steel would have. He gives you the ledger and whispers that forged raid orders are being sold like cattle.

nodes.label: Frightened Ink
text: Your hand on the hilt breaks his courage. He gives up the ledger, but his panic will run through the walls before dawn.

nodes.label: Old Postern
text: A narrow postern opens onto a deer trail behind the ridge. It is too small for a war band and therefore perfect for anyone not wishing to be remembered.

nodes.label: River Weather
text: The river road runs beside flooded fields and low stone tollhouses. Barges drag against the current like stubborn thoughts.

nodes.label: Ferry Calm
text: A ferrywoman carries you across a brown bend without asking more than your destination. That kind of mercy usually means she already knows enough.

nodes.label: Mired Wheel
text: A grain wagon sinks to its hubs. You spend half a ration and two hours helping strangers because hungry towns remember both cruelty and kindness.

nodes.label: River Patrol
text: Toll riders inspect saddlebags along the causeway. You pass, but one marks your cloak color on a wax tablet.

nodes.label: Stone Market
text: Stone Market stinks of fish oil, wet wool, and argument. Rumor says Mira Fen can move a priest through a locked gate and make the gate apologize.

nodes.label: Open Purse
text: You buy hard cheese and oats from a widow who weighs honestly after seeing the royal seal. That worries you more than cheating would have.

nodes.label: Mira's Boat
text: Mira Fen waits under a patched awning, boots on a coil of rope and a knife tucked where polite people keep prayer beads.

nodes.label: Gallows Crowd
text: A squire is being dragged toward the gallows for carrying false orders. He keeps shouting that the seal was real, even if the command was not.

nodes.label: Market Fork
text: Market noise folds around you. A guide might save time, dice might earn coin, and leaving now would keep your name from settling too deeply here.

nodes.label: Mira Deal
text: Mira names three prices for a quiet passage: coin, a useful secret, or the pleasure of refusing a royal errand to your face.

nodes.label: Condemned Squire
text: The squire sees the compact case and stops shouting. His lip is split, but his eyes are clear enough to understand what kind of road you are on.

nodes.label: River Guide
text: The guide takes your coin and gives you a reed-marked pass used by ferrymen who prefer profit to law. He also tells you which tollman drinks.

nodes.label: Dice Table
text: You sit at a barrel where boatmen throw bone dice and pretend every loss was nearly a win. The market leans closer.

nodes.label: Dice Win
text: The bones favor you. A boatman pays in clipped silver and a warning: someone has been asking after Maerla's courier.

nodes.label: Dice Loss
text: The dice betray you with cheerful indifference. Laughter follows as you leave the barrel poorer in coin and richer in attention.

nodes.label: Quiet Passage
text: Mira's skiff slips through willow shade and under a toll chain lifted by a boy who never looks up. The river keeps secrets if paid first.

nodes.label: Traded Name
text: You tell Mira which Brant steward sent false orders. She smiles once, sharp as a hook, and gives you the reed pass.

nodes.label: Leave Stalls
text: You leave the market before it can swallow the shape of your errand. Behind you, bells, haggling, and gallows boards keep arguing.

nodes.label: Loose Rope
text: You cut the squire free during a scuffle over spilled eels. He vanishes into the crowd, but not before swearing his sword to your need.

nodes.label: Last Words
text: The squire whispers that a hostage letter named Red Ford and a black banner. Then the guards drag him away before your face betrays the value of it.

nodes.label: Smuggler Cut
text: Mira's route leaves the honest road behind. Reeds scrape the boat, and every splash sounds briefly like a drawn blade.

nodes.label: Hidden Ford
text: Mira shows you a ford marked by three white stones under the water. It leads toward the marsh road that taxmen insist does not exist.

nodes.label: River Ambush
text: Two masked men rise from the reeds. Mira curses, you duck, and the skiff scrapes free after a brief, ugly exchange of steel.

nodes.label: Toll Bargain
text: A tollman spots the skiff. One coin and Mira's most insulting smile persuade him that he saw only fog.

nodes.label: River Fog
text: Fog thickens until the reeds become gray walls. In that hush, you hear an old marching song and somehow know which bend to trust.

nodes.label: River Choices
text: By dusk you stand where the river road splits toward the mills, the marsh, and the safer way back. Your boots smell permanently of wet rope.

nodes.label: Grey Mill
text: Grey Mill turns slowly in floodwater while men argue over grain owed to soldiers. Hunger has made everyone legal-minded.

nodes.label: Miller's Dilemma
text: The miller asks whether the compact will feed children or merely teach lords new words for taking bread. Around him, workers wait for your answer.

nodes.label: Grain Guard
text: You help divide the sacks under witness marks, enough for soldiers without starving the village. It is not justice, but it is better than appetite.

nodes.label: River Return
text: You leave the river country with mud drying on your cloak and rumors clinging beneath it. The main roads wait with new teeth.

nodes.label: Hill Weather
text: The abbey road climbs through thorn and sheep pasture. Above, Hollow Abbey keeps its windows narrow against wind, thieves, and perhaps memory.

nodes.label: Clear Bells
text: Abbey bells carry cleanly over the hills. For once, no one stops you before the gate, though the crows on the wall show more curiosity than monks.

nodes.label: Hungry Shrine
text: A wayside shrine shelters three hungry children and their grandmother. You leave food because the old gods and new both notice small accounts.

nodes.label: Pilgrim Trouble
text: A pilgrim recognizes Maerla's clasp on your cloak and asks too loudly whether the king truly died clean. The question runs ahead of you.

nodes.label: Hollow Abbey
text: Brother Caldus receives you in a hall lined with cracked royal tablets. The abbey smells of ink, beeswax, and winter stored in stone.

nodes.label: Caldus Speaks
text: Caldus says Maelor feared a council of swords less than a single smiling guardian. He wrote that fear in margins no court singer would copy.

nodes.label: Reliquary Dust
text: Inside a reliquary drawer, you find an iron key wrapped with a note: "For the oath beneath the oath." Monks are rarely as tidy as they pretend.

nodes.label: Fever Hall
text: You wash fevered faces and grind bitter leaves. A novice tells you the abbey's lower door opened by itself the night Maelor died.

nodes.label: Ink Room
text: Caldus unlocks the ink room. The dead king's hand appears in ledgers, private notes, and a half-drafted copy of the compact.

nodes.label: King's Margins
text: Maelor's notes name three forged letters and one lord who profited whenever border villages burned. The page is dry, but it feels freshly dangerous.

nodes.label: Treaty Draft
text: You copy the compact in a clean hand. If the original is stolen, ink may still carry a dead man's will where wax cannot.

nodes.label: Seal Test
text: The abbey keeps an older seal ring used for minority councils. Its mark matches Maelor's compact, which means the law has deeper roots than ambition.

nodes.label: Cloister Night
text: Night gathers in the cloister. Wind moves through the arches like a courtier touching every shoulder and naming no one.

nodes.label: Old Dream
text: You dream of oak roots under a throne and wake with a carved token in your fist. Caldus refuses to look surprised. 🌳

nodes.label: Knife Novice
text: A novice with frightened eyes tries to search your pack by moonlight. You stop him, but his little knife earns blood before tears.

nodes.label: Snowmelt Herbs
text: Behind the kitchen, snowmelt feeds a patch of stubborn herbs. Their smell is sharp enough to convince your body it still has work to do.

nodes.label: Lost Page
text: A loose page slides from a binding as if tired of hiding. It names Highmere's old council rite and the witness seats needed to make it bite.

nodes.label: Abbey Decision
text: Caldus points toward the crypt stair, then toward the border road. "Words rot if they never meet hunger," he says.

nodes.label: Crypt Stair
text: The iron key opens a door below the copy room. Cold air climbs around your boots, carrying the mineral smell of buried rain.

nodes.label: Stone Saints
text: Three old stone figures wait beneath the abbey: one holds a bowl, one a sword, one an empty map. Their faces have been worn soft by vows.

nodes.label: Mercy Oath
text: You swear that the heir will not be traded like a hostage if your hand can prevent it. The bowl fills with clear water from nowhere.

nodes.label: War Omen
text: You ask who wins if the houses draw steel. The sword figure weeps rust, and in the stain you recognize the shape of Red Ford.

nodes.label: Old Map
text: The empty map is not empty when candlelight strikes it sideways. Marsh causeways and postern tracks crawl into view like veins.

nodes.label: Crypt Exit
text: The crypt does not let travelers leave the same way twice. Stone clicks somewhere behind you, patient as law.

nodes.label: Calm Passage
text: A narrow passage returns you to the abbey garden under a sky rubbed clean by rain. Caldus waits with no questions he expects answered.

nodes.label: Loose Stones
text: A stair gives under your heel. You catch the wall, but the fall bruises your ribs and teaches you humility at speed.

nodes.label: Hidden Cache
text: Behind a saint's cracked foot, you find a pilgrim cache: two coins, dried apples, and a note thanking whoever needed them more.

nodes.label: Abbot's Warning
text: Caldus seals a warning for Highmere and asks whether the living still respect dead hands. His smile suggests he already knows the answer.

nodes.label: Sealed Warning
text: You tuck the abbot's warning beside the compact. It adds no weight, yet your coat hangs differently with another truth inside it.

nodes.label: Abbey Return
text: You descend from Hollow Abbey with ink on your cuff and hill wind in your lungs. Below, the roads have not grown kinder.

nodes.label: Border Weather
text: The road to Red Ford runs through burned fields and thin fences. Soldiers have passed here often enough that even scarecrows look enlisted.

nodes.label: Quiet Mile
text: The border road gives you a quiet mile, which feels less like peace than a room holding its breath.

nodes.label: Raider Sign
text: You find hoofprints arranged too neatly beside a burned shed. Real raiders do not usually compose evidence for audiences.

nodes.label: Refugee Line
text: A line of refugees shares the road, carrying pans, blankets, and a silence heavier than furniture. You help lift a child over a flooded ditch.

nodes.label: Red Ford
text: Red Ford is a camp of patched tents, cold cookfires, and soldiers pretending not to count the dead. Captain Dain Locke watches you arrive without blinking.

nodes.label: Dain's Measure
text: Dain reads Maelor's seal, then your face. "If that parchment feeds my soldiers lies," he says, "I will hang it beside the cooks."

nodes.label: Field Tents
text: You bind wounds and share what comfort you can. Men who expected orders receive attention instead, and that unsettles them into loyalty.

nodes.label: Ridge Scout
text: You climb the ridge above Red Ford. Smoke, hoofmarks, and banners arrange themselves below like a board game played by hungry men.

nodes.label: War Council
text: Dain's officers crowd around a barrel map. They have courage, bad boots, and too many reasons to believe the next rider brings betrayal.

nodes.label: Enemy Fires
text: From the ridge you see three campfires placed to seem like thirty. Whoever arranged them wants fear to travel faster than men.

nodes.label: Horse Fall
text: Your horse slips on shale and throws you hard. The beast limps away offended; you stand slower and with less pride.

nodes.label: Black Banner
text: In a ravine, you find a black banner hidden under brush, ready to be raised by men who want the next raid blamed on someone convenient.

nodes.label: Truce Speech
text: You argue that tired soldiers make poor kings and worse witnesses. Dain grunts, which his officers interpret as permission to keep listening.

nodes.label: Shield Drill
text: You spend an hour in the mud helping Dain's line close gaps. Practical competence does what speeches cannot.

nodes.label: False Raiders
text: You lay out the forged signs, the hostage letter, and the timing of burned farms. Dain's jaw tightens until the council falls quiet.

nodes.label: Camp Night
text: Night at Red Ford brings dice, coughing, whetstones, and men whispering the names of places they might never see again.

nodes.label: Friendly Watch
text: A veteran shares a cloak and a cup of barley beer. The warmth is thin, but thin warmth still counts on a border night.

nodes.label: Camp Thief
text: A boy tries to lift your purse near the horse lines. He freezes when you catch his wrist, already expecting the kind of justice camps teach quickly.

nodes.label: Raven Token
text: A messenger from Maerla finds you by the cookfires and gives you a black wax token. It will open one Highmere door or close one mouth.

nodes.label: Border Choice
text: By morning, Red Ford has given you mud, soldiers, and a clearer map of who profits from panic. Dain waits to see where you spend it.

nodes.label: Hard Chase
text: You chase the boy through guy ropes and cook smoke. He drops a stolen coin and escapes with your mercy, though your knee protests the pursuit.

nodes.label: Mercy Given
text: You let the boy keep his hand and his terror. By dawn, three soldiers know you are not the easiest kind of cruel.

nodes.label: Dain's Price
text: Dain says he can lend weight to your words, but not blindly. He wants either evidence he can defend or glory he can sell to frightened captains.

nodes.label: Shared Proof
text: You show Dain enough to make his anger disciplined. He names two officers who will stand with you at Highmere if they live to arrive.

nodes.label: Promised Glory
text: You promise Dain that the council will remember Red Ford. It is a useful promise, though promises have been known to sour in noble kitchens.

nodes.label: Border Return
text: You leave Red Ford while soldiers argue over breakfast and burial duty. Behind you, Dain's camp keeps holding the line because no one has relieved it.

nodes.label: Marsh Gate
text: The marsh path begins where honest roads give up. Reeds close around you, hiding sky, sound, and every witness who might have been useful.

nodes.label: Reed Path
text: The reeds part along a narrow strip of old stones. Someone built this path for messengers who were not supposed to exist.

nodes.label: Black Mud
text: Black mud takes your boot and nearly takes the rest of you. You get free by sacrificing food, dignity, and several excellent curses.

nodes.label: Hermit Fire
text: A hermit sits beside a peat fire, wearing a lord's old cloak turned inside out. He says he has been expecting anyone with enough trouble to find him.

nodes.label: Old Causeway
text: A cracked causeway surfaces beneath the water. Its stones bear council marks older than Highmere, proof that shared rule was not invented yesterday.

nodes.label: Marsh Camp
text: You make a small camp on a dry hump of grass. The old map, the hermit's smoke, and a risky reed-cut all offer ways through.

nodes.label: Hermit Bargain
text: The hermit knows a dry way to Highmere and has the manners of a man who once dined above salt. He asks what kind of guest you are.

nodes.label: Map Causeway
text: The old map leads you across stones hidden just below the water. Each step feels like following a secret the land is tired of keeping.

nodes.label: Reed Blades
text: You hack through reeds until your arms ache. The marsh charges blood for impatience, but it does eventually give way.

nodes.label: Bread Price
text: You share food. The hermit eats with courtly care, then draws a route on your sleeve in charcoal and refuses to explain why he knows it.

nodes.label: Guest Law
text: You show the oak token or lay guest bread between you. The hermit laughs softly and names the old council road by its forbidden name.

nodes.label: No Bargain
text: You leave the hermit with his fire and his secrets. Behind you he begins humming a tune that sounds uncomfortably like a funeral march.

nodes.label: Hidden Ford
text: The marsh thins near a ford under pale grass. Highmere's towers appear and vanish in fog, close enough to tempt mistakes.

nodes.label: Ford Success
text: You cross before the fog lifts. By the time Highmere's watch sees you, you are already on the lawful side of the ditch.

nodes.label: Ford Delay
text: A sunken branch tears your boot and costs you an hour. When you finally climb out, Highmere's outer watch has changed to less friendly faces.

nodes.label: Highmere Rise
text: Highmere stands on a chalk hill above roads from every rival house. Its banners hang wet and heavy, as if the whole march is holding its breath.

nodes.label: Gate Check
text: The gate captain asks for authority. Behind him, courtiers, captains, abbots, and merchants climb toward the moot hall where Princess Elowen waits.

nodes.label: Royal Entry
text: Maelor's seal opens the gate, though not every guard likes obeying a dead king. The captain sends a runner ahead to announce you.

nodes.label: Seal Entry
text: The old council seal makes the gate captain pale. He bows to law older than his employer and lets you pass without another word.

nodes.label: Postern Entry
text: You enter through a side postern with damp moss on your shoulder. It saves delay, but appearing from nowhere gives rumor a fine pair of boots.

nodes.label: Moot Hall
text: The moot hall is a forest of banners. Princess Elowen sits small beneath them, watching adults discuss her future as if she were a border crossing.

nodes.label: First Speech
text: You speak before the factions settle into formation. Surprise gives your words a narrow bridge over the first wave of scorn.

nodes.label: Listening Knives
text: You stay silent long enough to hear the room choose its masks. Some men posture for honor, some for fear, and a few for coin.

nodes.label: Banner Accusation
text: You lay the black banner before the hall. Its false colors make several honest men angry and several guilty men suddenly interested in the ceiling.

nodes.label: Council Bargains
text: The council fractures into offers. Garran wants a sword-backed regency, Maerla wants law, river voices want food, and Elowen wants someone to ask her a question.

nodes.label: Ledger Reading
text: You read names, sums, false orders, and paid fires until the hall stops breathing together. Truth enters like a cold guest and takes the best chair.

nodes.label: Oath Circle
text: You ask each faction to speak one oath aloud before the heir. The old hall was built for this; even proud voices sound smaller inside it.

nodes.label: Final Claim
text: At last the compact, the gathered proof, and your bruised road all point toward a choice. Elowen looks at you, not the banners.

nodes.label: Steel Vote
text: The hall leans toward steel because steel gives frightened people something simple to admire. Garran waits, expression carved from weather and appetite.

nodes.label: Compact Holds
text: The compact is read under royal seal, abbey witness, river mark, and border oath. No one loves the settlement enough to trust it, which is why it might survive.
Elowen names her own council seat before the hall can forget she has a voice. Harrowmere leaves Highmere bruised, wary, and still whole.

nodes.label: Armed Regency
text: You back an armed regency with Garran's banners and Dain's hard-eyed soldiers binding the hall. The roads quiet within a fortnight.
Peace arrives wearing mail. It protects Elowen, but every rescued village learns to listen for hooves before bells.

nodes.label: Ledger Court
text: The black ledger becomes a public wound. Lords fall, captains swear innocence, and merchants discover that ink can hang a man as neatly as rope.
The compact survives in argument rather than ceremony. Harrowmere does not heal quickly, but at least it now knows where the knife entered.

nodes.label: Free Road
text: You refuse to become the hand that crowns another arrangement of hungry names. With copy, witness, or memory enough to matter, you take the compact back to the roads.
Behind you, Highmere keeps shouting. Ahead, smaller halls wait, and sometimes history enters by the kitchen door.

nodes.label: Broken Road
text: The road finally spends what your body could not afford. Fever, blood loss, or plain exhaustion pulls you down before Highmere's towers rise.
A farmer finds the compact case under your cloak and hides it from the next patrol. Not every failed errand is finished.

nodes.label: Hunted Courier
text: Suspicion closes the gates before you can reach the moot. Patrols compare notes, tollmen remember your face, and someone with cleaner gloves takes the compact.
Harrowmere still gathers at Highmere, but your truth arrives late, translated by enemies.
